vote.proposed_artifact:
DECISION: Represent an Azure NSG as a real, shared policy resource managed in a policy rail/library and displayed on canvas as compact semantic attachment badges on its actual association targets, subnets and NICs, with on-demand non-routing association lines, optional scope overlay, and inspector-based editing, effective-rule aggregation, and blast radius; no generic peer-node card or traffic-style edge is used for NSGs.

CONCEPTUAL MODEL AND VISUAL HIERARCHY
1. Topology layer: deployable resources (VMs, VNets, subnets, NICs) and their explicit connections.
2. Containment layer: subnets/VNets rendered as containers or boundary shapes.
3. Policy attachment layer: NSG badges on the boundary of a subnet or on the NIC card. A badge is shield+name+state and is not a connection port; it has no generic all-side handles.
4. Detail layer: inspector and policy rail; focus or expand can temporarily show a full policy card for an NSG so it can be edited without pretending it is a topology peer.
The subnet-level versus NIC-level distinction is always explicit: badge text includes 'subnet' or 'NIC'. A VM glyph never receives an NSG badge unless the model explicitly materializes a NIC inside it; in that case the badge goes on the NIC node.

INTERACTIONS
Add: Catalog or Add Security Policy creates an unattached NSG in the policy rail. The user can immediately choose a target via an Attach to... target picker that lists only valid subnets/NICs.
Attach: either from the NSG in the rail (Attach to... then click a valid target) or from a target badge (Add security policy then choose an NSG). Invalid targets are not selectable; the picker filters by resource type and region; no generic connection drag is required and none is offered for NSG-to-VM.
Select: selecting a badge or rail item highlights every association for that NSG on the canvas and fills the inspector with association count, target list, rules summary, state, and blast radius.
Inspect: inspector shows source/provenance (created locally vs imported/unknown), rule summaries, all association targets (type, name, region), effective security per target, conflicting/effective concerns, and validation state.
Edit: edits happen in the inspector or policy rail; renaming or changing rules updates every target badge; before applying an edit, a blast radius preview lists affected targets.
Detach: Detach in inspector removes only that NSG-target association; the NSG remains in the rail if it has other associations, or becomes unattached. Detach is undoable.
Reuse: an NSG can be attached to any number of subnets/NICs; the rail shows association count. Selection highlights all target badges. Duplicate attach to the same target is prevented.
Delete: delete from inspector/rail after confirmation. Confirmation lists every target and the effect of rule loss; if any target is unresolved/imported, the confirmation warns that the association cannot be restored in the persisted editor state. Delete is undoable within the editor session and restorable from migration snapshot after session.

SUBNET VS NIC
A subnet badge sits on the subnet boundary and is marked subnet. A NIC badge sits on the NIC card and is marked NIC. The canvas never draws an NSG-to-VM edge. For a VM with multiple NICs, each NIC can have its own badges and effective view; the VM card shows only a summary count like '2 NICs with NSGs' if needed, not an NSG itself. A subnet association is inherited by every workload in that subnet; the inspector labels the inherited layer as subnet-level and aggregates it with NIC-level rules. Effective rules are shown per target in the inspector by merging subnet-level and NIC-level rules in Azure documented order, with a link to provider documentation rather than a formal evaluation engine.

CANVAS / CATALOG / INSPECTOR
Default canvas: badges only; no association lines or overlays. Badges collapse to shield+count at low zoom.
Relationships mode: shows non-routing association lines between the NSG rail item and its target badges, or directly between badges; lines are dashed, arrowless, gray, labeled attached on hover/focus, and off by default to avoid traffic-path confusion.
Scope overlay (optional): for a selected subnet-associated NSG, a translucent outline around all affected subnets; shown on demand only so it does not imply stronger isolation than the rules.
Catalog/rail: list of all NSGs with name, target count, and validation state; supports search/filter; is the single home for shared policy identity.
Inspector: contextual detail; no NSG rule contents on canvas, but a summary and View rules affordance.

VALIDATION STATES
Use four mutually distinct states, each represented by icon + text, not color alone:
incomplete: NSG exists but has no rules or missing required region/scope data.
invalid: association target is missing, wrong type, or stale; attach attempts are filtered first, but imported/legacy data can still be invalid.
conflicting/effective-policy concern: subnet and NIC associations or overlapping rules create a conflict or aggregated effective-rule concern; not necessarily invalid but flagged for review.
unknown/provider-unverified: imported target or provider verification is pending/unknown; UI says the value is not verified and does not claim an effective result.

ACCESSIBILITY
Every badge, rail row, and inspector control is a real focusable element with visible focus.
Keyboard: Tab moves through canvas and rail; Enter/Space opens badge menu; A opens attach picker when focus is on an NSG or target; X opens detach; Delete opens delete confirmation; Esc closes overlays.
Screen reader: badges announce name, type, association level (subnet or NIC), state, and association count; ARIA live regions announce attach, detach, delete, update, and validation changes.
Color independence: icons and text carry state; no state depends only on color.
Target size: interactive badges and controls have at least 44x44 CSS px when feasible and never smaller than 24x24 CSS px per WCAG 2.5.8; zoomed-out collapsed badges maintain a visible target size and contrast. Exact tokens are delegated to the design system.

WIREFRAME (TEXTUAL)
Left rail:
[+ Add Security Policy]
allow-web   Azure NSG  [2 targets] [Valid]
deny-load   Azure NSG  [1 target]  [Conflict]
Canvas:
+------------------------------------------------+
| subnet prod-web   [allow-web subnet]           |
|   VM app-01                                    |
|     NIC eth0 [allow-web NIC]                    |
|   VM app-02                                    |
+------------------------------------------------+
Inspector: allow-web
Associations: subnet prod-web (subnet); app-01/eth0 (NIC)
Effective security for app-01/eth0: view aggregated rules
Blast radius: 2 targets
[Edit] [Detach] [Delete]

COMPATIBILITY AND MIGRATION
Existing saved diagrams that encode NSG as a peer node are migrated by a one-time conversion: find NSG cards, read their saved association edges, and convert them into semantic associations (target type derived from edge target) plus rail entries and target badges.
If an edge points to a VM instead of a subnet/NIC, the converter does NOT silently rewrite it to a NIC; it creates an invalid/unresolved state and prompts the user to re-target, so domain accuracy is not guessed.
Migration is non-destructive: original serialized diagram is preserved in an undo snapshot and an exportable backup; rollback restores the previous peer-node representation without data loss.
During the transition window, the editor accepts and exports both the original peer-node form and the new semantic form.

FAILURE PATHS, ROLLBACK, STOP CONDITIONS, RETAINED UNKNOWNS, SCOPE EXCLUSIONS, RISKS, ADVERSARIAL CHECKS
Failure: an imported edge targets an object that no longer exists, producing an unresolved placeholder with invalid state; user can reattach or delete with confirmation.
Failure: provider verification API is unavailable, producing unknown state; UI never claims verified effective rules; no write is attempted from this design.
Failure: a reused NSG is edited and the update fails partway; transaction-style rollback restores prior badge/rule state and shows an error.
Rollback: undo stack and migration snapshot cover attach, detach, edit, and delete of NSGs; delete of a reused NSG can be undone in the session and restored from backup after the session.
Stop conditions: proposal stops at design contract; no editor code, catalog overhaul, rule-authoring UX, or design-system token selection is written here.
Retained unknowns: current editor persistence schema, graph API, and exact Connect mode behavior are not present in the repository evidence and must be mapped during implementation; Azure effective-rule evaluation and conflict priority are referenced to provider docs and may be surfaced as text until an evaluation engine is contracted.
Risks: additional states may be harder to teach; mitigated by compact default, discoverable relationships mode, and a short onboarding hint. Scope overlays might imply stronger protection; mitigated by on-demand display and legend text that NSGs filter traffic, not isolate it. Badges on many targets could clutter; mitigated by counts and zoom collapse.
Adversarial checks: no arrowheads or routing lines appear by default for NSGs; no direct NSG-to-VM attach is possible; an NSG cannot be presented as forwarding traffic; a badge is never a generic connection handle; shared identity is never duplicated into independent cards; a deleted NSG shows blast radius before confirmation; unknown targets are never presented as verified; NIC versus subnet distinction is always labeled and machine-readable.

OPTION LEDGER
A (typed peer node): pruned as primary because even a specialized node keeps NSG in topology space, implies peer-like connectivity, and wastes canvas; retained only as fallback rendering for legacy diagrams during migration.
B (attached badge): retained as primary canvas representation because it is semantically correct, compact, and progressive; duplication risk is solved by central policy rail and inspector identity.
C (scope overlay): retained as an on-demand visualization only, not the main representation, because it strongly shows subnet coverage but poorly fits NIC-level association and can imply isolation.
D (association edge): retained only in on-demand Relationships mode with arrowless dashed style, because default lines risk traffic-path confusion and spaghetti under reuse.
E (policy rail/library): retained as the management surface paired with badges, because it preserves shared-resource identity, search, and blast radius.
F (hybrid progressive disclosure): selected; it combines B, D, C, and E with a compact default and explicit states; Option A is not part of the primary model.
required_changes: Adopt Option F as the primary decision and prune Option A as the primary representation
During implementation, map the existing saved peer-node edges to semantic association records with an unambiguous target-type rule; do not guess VM-to-NIC conversions
Add a concise data-model and effective-rule mapping note to the implementation contract before engineering starts

AC4: attach flows use filtered target pickers, invalid targets are unselectable, and no generic NSG-to-VM edge exists
AC5: default canvas has badges only; rules, provenance, conflicts, effective security, and relationships appear on demand
AC6: keyboard, screen-reader, focus, target size, and color-independent state behavior are specified
AC7: migration converts peer-node edges to semantic associations, keeps original snapshot, and provides rollback
AC8: validation distinguishes incomplete, invalid, conflicting/effective-policy concern, and unknown/provider-unverified

vote.summary: Propose hybrid progressive-disclosure model (Option F): NSGs become shared policy resources in a policy rail/inspector and appear on canvas only as compact, typed attachment badges on subnets and NICs, with on-demand arrowless association lines and optional scope overlays. This keeps security visible, preserves reuse and blast radius, prevents invalid NSG-to-VM connections, and is migration-safe; the generic peer-node card is pruned as the primary representation.
